Civil Revision No. 27 of 1989 (Barisal)
Civil Revision No. 2938 of 1991 (Dhaka)
lawyer:
Abdul Quayum, Advocate — For the Petitioner. 
Chandi Charan Paul, Advocate — For the Opposite Party Nos 1 and 2.
parties:
Abdul Malek Majhee ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Apser Ali Howlader and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
A.K. Badrul Huq, J: Feeling aggrieved by a judgment passed by the appellate Court allowing appeal on reversing the judgment passed by the trial Court dismissing pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the pre-emptor approached this Court in an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure whereupon Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 10-9-88 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Pirojpur in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 22 of 1986 should not be set aside. 

 2. The only question which falls for determination in this Rule is whether clause (a) of sub-section 10 of section 96 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act stands as a bar for the pre-emptor to preempt the land under the deed of transfer in favour of the pre-emptee who became a co-sharer in the tenancy by way of inheritance not on the date of transfer but subsequent to the date of transfer. 

 The petitioner as pre-emptor instituted Miscellaneous Case No. 6 of 1984 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Kowkhali Upazila under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for pre-empting the land under the deed of sale dated 1-7-1978 on the ground that he is a non-notified co-sharer by inheritance and he for the first time on 2-10-79 became aware of the kabala under the miscellaneous proceeding and thereafter filed the case. 

 4. The opposite party Nos.1 and 2 being pre-emptees resisted the case by filing written objection taking the ground that the application for pre-emption was not maintainable as because they became co-sharers by way of inheritance. It was pleaded that the transferor opposite parties who were co-sharers by inheritance having died subsequent to the kabala deed under the pre-emption proceeding, they became co-sharers by way of inheritance and they were protected under section 96(10)(a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the pre-emption case was not maintainable. 

 6. The pre-emptees felt aggrieved by the said decision and sought setting aside the same through a medium of appeal before the learned District Judge, Pirojpur. The appellate Court although concurred with the finding arrived at by the trial Court that the petitioner was a co-sharer by way of inheritance and that the case was not barred by limitation, set aside the judgment of the trial Court with the findings that the pre-emptees acquired the status of co-sharership by way of inheritance on the death of their predecessor Hamejuddin and Alikjan, the transferors and hence they were protected under section 96(10)(a) of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 8. Mr Abdul Quayum, learned Advocate for the pre-emptor petitioner appearing in support of the Rule, contended that the pre-emptee opposite parties were not co-sharers on the date of the deed of transfer and in the event of any change of status of co-sharership of the pre-emptees, the right of pre-emption accrued to the pre-emptor would not be affected. The further contention of the learned Advocate is that, the acquisition of interest by the pre-emptees subsequent to the impugned kabala cannot take away the right of pre-emption of the pre-emptor and the lower appellate Court misdirected itself in its total approach of the matter and committed a substantial error of law in finding that in view of the bar under section 96 (10)(a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the pre-emption case was not maintainable against the pre-emptess. In support of the contention reliance had been placed in the case of Abdul Baten vs. Abdul Latif Sheikh and others reported in 45 DLR (AD) 26. In the said case the Appellate Division held that the right of pre-emption accrued to the pre-emptor is not affected by the subsequent acquisition of co-sharership by the pre-emptor. 

 11. To appreciate the rival contentions advanced by the learned Advocates of both the sides, it will be appropriate to notice the provisions of section 96(10)(a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and sections 47 and 60 of the Registration Act which read as follows respectively : 

 Section 96(10) (a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 Section 96(10) Nothing in this section shall apply to (a) a transfer to a co-sharer in the tenancy whose interest has accrued otherwise than by purchase. Sections 47 and 60 of the Registration Act : 

 12. Clause (a) of sub-section 10 of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act lays down that a transfer to a co-sharer whose interest in the land transferred has accrued by inheritance is not liable to pre-emption. 

 17. Section 47 of the Registration Act governs from which point of time the title will vest with a party and got no bearing on the question of accrual of the right of pre-emption. In the case of Abdul Baten vs. Abdul Latif Sheikh and others, 45 DLR (AD) 26 referred to by the learned Advocate for the petitioner, the interpretation of clause (a) of sub-section 10 of section 96 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came up for consideration before their Lordships of the Appellate Division. The Appellate Division held: "The right of pre-emption accrued to the pre-emptor is not affected by subsequent acquisition of co-sharership by the pre-emptee". In deciding the said case application of section 47 of the Registration Act along with clause (a) of sub-section 10 of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act did not come up for consideration before their Lordships. 

 18. This question came up for consideration before their Lordships of the Appellate Division in the case of Ayesha Khatun (Musammat) vs. Musammat Jahanara Begum and others reported in 43 DLR (AD) 9 wherein interpretation of both the sections 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and 47 of the Registration Act was involved. The observations of their Lordships of the Appellate Division are covered in the following terms : "It is now a settled principle of law that the cause of action under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act accrues on the date of registration of the deed of sale, when registration is compulsory. This is because the right of pre-emption arises on the completion of the transfer. It could not be said to have been completed earlier by reason of section 47 of the Registration Act though there-under the instrument of transfer commences to operate from earlier date. "Mr Abdul Quayum with all fairness submitted before me that in view of the said decision of the Appellate Division, he cannot now say that he got a point to be decided in favour of the pre-emptor. 

 19. In view of the discussion made hereinabove and also viewed in the light of the aforesaid principle of law enunciated by our Appellate Division I am of the considered view that clause (a) of sub-section 10 of section 96 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act stands as a bar on the part of the pre-emptor to maintain his application against the pre-emptee who acquired the status of a co-sharership by way of inheritance before the deed of transfer under the pre-emption proceeding was registered. The judgment of the appellate Court is well founded on law and the same does not warrant any interference by this court in the exercise of the power under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The Rule is devoid of any substance and the same, thus, is liable to be discharged.
